props.title: 102 Not Out
props.initialSlug: 102-year-old dad teaches his 75-year-old son to live

sections.content: **102 Not Out (2018)** (2018) marks a fascinating entry in Indian cinema's exploration of intergenerational relationships, starring Amitabh Bachchan as a 102-year-old father and Rishi Kapoor as his 75-year-old son. The film follows similar emotional territory as **The Bucket List** (2007) and **Nebraska** (2013), examining life's later chapters with both humor and heart. Like Piku (2015), another brilliant Bachchan performance dealing with parent-child dynamics, it manages to find lightness in potentially heavy subject matter.

sections.content: The film taps into a rich vein of recent Indian cinema examining aging and family bonds. **The Lunchbox** (2013) explored loneliness in later life through an accidental friendship, while **Badhaai Ho** (2018) used comedy to tackle ageism and late-life romance. **102 Not Out** stands out for refusing to treat its elderly characters as purely tragic or comic relief figures, instead giving them full agency and complex emotional lives. SUBHEAD: Breaking Age Stereotypes in Cinema

What makes **102 Not Out** particularly significant is how it challenges traditional film depictions of the elderly. Unlike the patronizing tone of many "old age" comedies like **The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel** (2011), it presents its centenarian protagonist as vibrant and purposeful. This aligns it more with films like **Amour** (2012) and **Youth** (2015) that treat aging with nuance and dignity, while maintaining its distinctly Indian perspective on family dynamics and filial duty.
